h1: The 6 Best 21-Inch Lawn Mowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six 21-inch cordless lawn mowers from EGO, Greenworks, Worx and SENIX, with plain advice on battery size, drive and mulching.
summary: The Greenworks 80V self-propelled is our top pick for medium to larger lawns where walking effort matters. The EGO Power+ LM2114 is the push option for a standard lawn, and the Worx WG752 is the one to buy if you switch between mulching and bagging. The SENIX X6 packs the biggest battery here.
intro: A 21-inch deck is the common size because it balances cutting width against storage and handling. The real decision is not width, it is the battery, since the voltage and amp-hour rating decide how long you can mow and which other tools the pack will power.

Every mower here is cordless and has a 21-inch deck, so we ranked them on battery size, drive type, extras like mulching or height settings, and what each includes in the box. The order comes from the listings and from how owners describe these machines, with no runtime figures invented.

products.name: Greenworks 80V 21-Inch Self-Propelled Mower
products.verdict: Battery power and a drive system that does the walking for you.
products.description:
This mower pairs the 21-inch deck with an 80V system, a 4.0Ah battery and charger in the box, and self-propelled drive. It falls in the $200 to $500 range.

It takes first place because self-propel is the feature that most changes a mowing session on a larger lot, and the kit arrives complete. The push version below drops the drive but keeps the same battery, so this is the one to choose if the yard has length or a slope.

Buy it for medium to larger lawns. The caveat is cost, as you pay for the drive system, and one 4.0Ah pack limits a very large job.
products.idealFor: Medium to larger lawns where walking effort matters.
products.skipIf: Your lawn is small, flat and easy to push across.

products.name: EGO Power+ LM2114 21-Inch Cordless Mower
products.verdict: A straightforward full-width push mower on a 56V platform.
products.description:
The LM2114 uses a 21-inch deck on the 56V EGO battery platform, with a push drive and the battery and charger included. It also lands in the $200 to $500 range.

It places second because it lacks drive, which the Greenworks self-propelled version offers, but it keeps the setup simple for a standard lawn. Its 56V platform also lets you add other tools in that family later.

Choose it for an average, mostly flat yard. The caveat is plain: you push the whole way, and hills get tiring.
products.skipIf: Your lawn has slopes or is large.

products.name: SENIX X6 60V 21-Inch Self-Propelled Mower
products.verdict: An 8Ah pack, seven height levels and a smart display.
products.description:
The X6 runs on a 60V system with an 8Ah battery, the largest in this ranking, plus self-propelled drive, seven-level height adjustment and a smart display. It sits in the $200 to $500 range.

It lands third because it has the best spec sheet but the least established brand here, so there is less owner history to lean on. Against the Greenworks 80V self-propelled, you gain battery capacity and fine height control.

It suits buyers who value features over brand heritage. The caveat is that the smart display adds a component that could age, and long-term support is harder to judge.
products.idealFor: Feature-focused buyers with a larger lawn.
products.skipIf: You prefer a long-established mower brand.

products.name: Worx WG752 40V 21-Inch 3-in-1 Mower
products.verdict: Switches between mulching, bagging and side discharge.
products.description:
The WG752 has a 21-inch deck on a 40V platform and offers 3-in-1 operation: mulch, bag or side discharge. The listing rates it for up to half an acre, and it lands in the $200 to $500 range.

It ranks fourth because the 40V platform is a step below the 56V to 80V rivals, and the listing does not mention drive. The flexibility to change how clippings are handled is the draw.

Choose it for lawns where you mulch in summer and bag in autumn. The caveat is the smaller battery platform.
products.idealFor: Lawns that need flexible clipping handling.
products.skipIf: You want self-propel or the biggest battery.

products.name: Greenworks 60V 21-Inch Push Mower
products.verdict: A larger included battery for flat to gently sloped yards.
products.description:
A 21-inch push mower on a 60V system with a 5.0Ah battery and charger included. It lands in the $200 to $500 range.

It ranks fifth because it asks you to push, and the 80V Greenworks models offer similar kit with a different platform. What it offers over the EGO is a 5.0Ah pack, which suits longer sessions on a gentle slope.

Pick it if pack size matters more than drive. The caveat is that it has no self-propel for hills.

products.name: Greenworks 80V 21-Inch Push Mower
products.verdict: The 80V platform without paying for self-propel.
products.description:
This Greenworks has a 21-inch deck, an 80V system with a 4.0Ah battery and charger in the box, and a push drive. It lands in the $200 to $500 range.

It ranks last because the self-propelled sibling has the same battery and adds drive, and the 60V push mower brings a larger pack. It is a value play for those who want 80V tools.

Buy it if you plan to share the battery with other 80V tools. The caveat is that nothing here stands out beyond the platform.
products.skipIf: You want drive or a bigger battery.

methodology.title: Battery capacity
methodology.description: Voltage and amp-hours decide how much lawn one charge can cover, so battery size carried the most weight.

methodology.title: Drive type
methodology.description: Self-propelled versus push changes effort on larger or sloped lawns.

methodology.title: Platform value
methodology.description: Shared batteries across tools lower long-run cost, so platform breadth earned points.

methodology.title: Kit completeness
methodology.description: Included batteries and chargers separated finished kits from bare machines.

methodology.title: Features
methodology.description: Mulching modes, height levels and displays added points where the listing names them.

whatMatters.detail: Volts describe the platform and amp-hours describe capacity, much like a fuel tank. A bigger Ah number means a longer mowing session. Look for both figures in the title or bullets.
Self-propelled mowers drive their own wheels, which helps on larger or sloped lawns. Push mowers cost less. Check the drive type in the specs.
Buying into a battery family ties future tools to the same brand. That can be good or limiting. Check which other tools use the same voltage.
Mulching, bagging and side discharge each suit different seasons. A 3-in-1 deck handles all of them. Look for the words mulch and bag.
More cutting height levels let you tune for grass type and season. Seven levels is finer than the typical few. Look for the level count.

howToChoose.intro: Size and slope decide whether drive is worth paying for.

cards.label: Self-propelled
cards.text: Drives its own wheels and saves effort. The Greenworks 80V Self-Propelled and SENIX X6 are the picks.

cards.label: Push
cards.text: Simpler and lighter in cost. The EGO LM2114 and both Greenworks push models lead.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to push unless the lawn is large or sloped.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A 3-in-1 deck that mulches, bags or discharges to the side.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Worx WG752 lists all three modes.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Your lawn is large. The SENIX X6 offers the biggest battery and Greenworks 80V adds drive.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The lawn is flat. The Greenworks 60V Push gives a good battery for less.

faq.q: Does a 21-inch deck fit most yards?
faq.a: It suits average yards well. Smaller lots can use a narrower deck, while very large lawns might prefer more battery capacity.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake buying a battery mower?
faq.a: Ignoring the battery platform. Voltage decides which other tools you can share it with.

faq.q: Is self-propel worth the extra cost?
faq.a: On slopes or long lawns, yes. On flat small ones, push is plenty.

faq.q: Do all of these include a charger?
faq.a: The EGO and Greenworks listings state that the battery and charger are included. Check the Worx and SENIX pages to confirm.

faq.q: How do I store a battery mower?
faq.a: Keep the battery indoors away from extreme heat or cold, and charge it periodically during off-season storage.
The Worx WG752 lists mulch, bag or side discharge. Check others on their pages.

finalTake: For most larger lawns, the Greenworks 80V self-propelled is the best 21-inch mower on the list. The EGO LM2114 is the easy push choice for a standard yard, and the Worx WG752 wins on clipping flexibility. The SENIX X6 offers the largest battery.
